title: Kubernetes Core Architecture, Workloads & RBAC
summary: Master control plane components (apiserver, etcd, scheduler, controller-manager), Deployments, StatefulSets, ConfigMaps, Secrets, Probes, Scaling, and RBAC.
learningObjectives: Deploy, scale, and roll out high-availability multi-replica Deployments with zero downtime.
Configure least-privilege Role-Based Access Control (ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding).
Manage workload configuration via ConfigMaps, Secrets, and resource requests/limits.

curriculumModules.title: Control Plane Reconciliation & Workload Controllers
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: kube-apiserver is the sole component talking to etcd. Controllers watch API state and reconcile desired state: Deployment manages ReplicaSets, which manage Pods scheduled by kube-scheduler.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Always run stateless services with `replicas >= 3` spread across availability zones, paired with readinessProbes and CPU/Memory requests.

curriculumModules.title: Kubernetes RBAC Least-Privilege Authorization
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Kubernetes has no static user objects; it binds Subjects (User, Group, ServiceAccount) to Roles (namespace-scoped) or ClusterRoles (cluster-wide) via RoleBindings.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Disable `automountServiceAccountToken` by default and grant each workload a dedicated `ServiceAccount` bound to a namespace-scoped `Role`.

labs.title: High-Availability Deployment Scaling & Service Exposure
labs.scenario: Your e-commerce platform is preparing for a flash sale. Deploy `payments-api` in `production`, scale it to 3 replicas for multi-AZ resilience, and expose it on port 8080.
labs.productionContext: Production tiers require at least 3 replicas across zones and a backing Service to survive single-node failures without dropping requests.
objectives: Expose `payments-api` as a Service on port 8080 in `production`
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payments-api
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payments-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payments-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: payments-api
          image: nginx:1.27-alpine

steps.title: Expose Payments Service on Port 8080
steps.instruction: Expose `deployment/payments-api` as a ClusterIP service on port 8080 in `production`.

validationRules.description: Deployment production/payments-api has at least 3 ready replicas
validationRules.name: payments-api
validationRules.remediation: Create and scale deployment payments-api to 3 replicas in namespace production.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Verify both `kubectl get deploy payments-api -n production` (3/3 READY) and `kubectl get svc payments-api -n production`.

labs.title: Configuring Least-Privilege RBAC (ServiceAccount, Role & RoleBinding)
labs.scenario: An internal diagnostics pod in `production` needs read-only access to inspect pods without using the default cluster-admin credentials.
labs.productionContext: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark Section 5.1 mandates dedicated ServiceAccounts with minimal namespace-scoped Role permissions.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: diag-reader-sa
  namespace: production
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: pod-reader-role
  namespace: production
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: pod-reader-binding
  namespace: production
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure `diag-reader-sa`, `pod-reader-role`, and `pod-reader-binding` are all created inside namespace `production`.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which Kubernetes control plane component is the ONLY service that communicates directly with the etcd key-value datastore?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Only kube-apiserver reads from and writes to etcd; all other components watch and mutate cluster state exclusively through kube-apiserver.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the difference between a Kubernetes `Role` and a `ClusterRole`?
options: A Role is scoped to a single namespace, whereas a ClusterRole can grant permissions across all namespaces or cluster-scoped resources
A Role only applies to human users, whereas a ClusterRole only applies to ServiceAccounts
A Role requires a restart of kube-apiserver to take effect
There is no difference; Role is just an alias for ClusterRole
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Roles are namespace-scoped RBAC definitions, whereas ClusterRoles define permissions for cluster-scoped objects (like Nodes) or across all namespaces.
